That's why the numbers land where they do — 49.6% for Aatrox overall in this lane across 27,055 games, but a 50.5% head-to-head over 600 games with the lane edge going to Aatrox even though solo-kill odds and overall shape are dead even.

The 48.7% head-to-head over 378 games and Sett's lane and solo-kill edge confirm the early lane is genuinely his, but Fiora's itemized spike from Ravenous Hydra into Trinity Force flips extended skirmishes from level 9-13 onward.

brief.thesis: Camille's kit is built to dictate when trades happen: Q (Precision Protocol) extends her auto-attack range and her double-cast E (Hookshot) gives her both engage and disengage, so she picks the fights, not you. That's why Camille holds lane advantage and the solo-kill edge in this matchup even though the overall win rate sits at a close 46.3% over 863 games. Garen's only counters are timing E (Judgment) for the armor/MR buff before she commits, and holding Q (Decisive Strike) to silence her mid-combo instead of using it on cooldown.

yourWindow.when: Her E (Hookshot) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: If she's just used E to reposition, farm, or poke, she has no gap-close or disengage. Pop E (Judgment) for the armor/MR buff and walk into her — she cannot kite a spin she can't escape.

Garen's own Q (Decisive Strike) silences her, and a silenced champion cannot activate Riposte — so every real trade should open Q into E, never E first. Outside that window Fiora holds the edge in prolonged 1v1s because her passive (Duelist's Dance) stacks true damage and healing off revealed vitals, which lines up with her measured solo-kill advantage.

playing.title: Leap onto minions to engage pre-6
playing.detail: Camille has no hard engage before level 6, so use Leap Strike (Q) onto a minion to close distance and force her to react before she can set up her own combo.

playing.title: Freeze early, shove after Trinity
playing.detail: Hold the wave near your tower through levels 1-5 to deny her cs and bait a desperate Wall Dive into your stun; once Trinity Force completes, push to threaten plates instead.

playing.title: Respect Hextech Ultimatum after 6
playing.detail: Her R (Hextech Ultimatum) can leash you in place from range once she hits level 6 — don't overstay near walls or brush inside her ult range, and keep Flash for repositioning, not engaging.

playing.title: Convert stuns into kills with Ignite
playing.detail: The moment your Counter Strike lands, burn Ignite — her low base HP pool empties fast under Empower (W) plus Ignite, matching the measured solo-kill edge in this matchup.

playing.title: Track Trinity Force timing as your spike
playing.detail: Your dueling advantage jumps hardest once Trinity Force is complete, typically levels 9-13; play for trades around this item spike rather than forcing all-ins beforehand.

verdict.line: You lose if you trade into Garen's Q window before level 6; you win if you survive to Trinity Force and take it to sidelanes late.

brief.thesis: Garen's damage is almost entirely ability-based — Decisive Strike's bonus proc, the Judgment spin, and the Demacian Justice execute — none of which Counter Strike (E) actually blocks, since it only negates basic attacks. That single fact is why Jax sits at 43.8% over 1,177 games here despite a 50% average win rate: the champion's core defensive tool is nearly dead weight against this specific kit until items catch up.

theirWindow.when: Q up, wave pushing into you
theirWindow.what: This is his all-in: Q silence removes your ability to Leap Strike away or Counter Strike proactively, then he free-casts Judgment twice and autos through the silence. Do not stand and trade here — walk to the edge of minion range and let the wave die down instead.

yourWindow.when: Q on cooldown (post-trade)
yourWindow.what: Without the silence he can't punish your ability usage, so this is when you actually use Leap Strike to reposition onto him and weave autos for Relentless Assault stacks. Save Counter Strike for when he's about to auto you, not for his spell rotation.

verdict.line: You lose if Renekton lands his Fury-empowered all-ins between levels 2 and 5 uncontested, and you win once Grandmaster's Might (R) and a completed Trinity Force let you out-trade him from level 6 on.

brief.thesis: Renekton wins this lane on stat checks, not tricks: his Fury-empowered Q (Cull the Meek), W (Ruthless Predator), and E (Slice and Dice) combo out-damages and out-sustains anything Jax has before level 6, which is exactly why OP.GG lists him with lane advantage even though the matchup sits at only 49.8% over 666 games. brief.thesis: Aatrox's power is front-loaded: his W (Infernal Chains) root plus a fully-refreshed 2-charge Q chain and Deathbringer Stance passive let him bully every trade from level 1 through 5, which is exactly why OP.GG marks this as his lane. Sett has no answer to that chain until E and R come online, so the matchup is a race — survive his early spike, then use your W's charge-up to punish his most committed animation (his third Q swing) and flip the fight once your first item lands.

yourWindow.when: Aatrox has burned both Q charges
yourWindow.what: He has nothing left but autos and his E dash for several seconds. Walk him down, full-charge W (Haymaker), and follow with E (Facebreaker) — he cannot trade back until Q refreshes.

runes.keystoneWhy: This page measures 55.4% win rate here — the third-hit burst lets you win short, sharp trades before he ever reaches 50 Fury, which is exactly the window you control.

summoners.why: 91.6% pick rate at 50.6% win rate — Ignite punishes his Cull the Meek healing directly and gives you kill pressure the moment his empowered-W all-in window closes.

playing.title: Don't feed his Fury bar
playing.detail: Every auto and Q he lands on you builds toward the 50-Fury threshold. Give up minions rather than trade autos with him level 1-2 if you don't have to.

playing.title: Hold E for a real stun
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are on opposite sides of you — against a lone Renekton it just slows. Use minion positioning or wait for a real trade before committing it.

playing.title: Bank Grit before you punch
playing.detail: Haymaker stores damage you take as Grit passively. Let a poke or two land, then cash it in for the shield and true-damage burst rather than using W on cooldown.

playing.title: Walk him down after his E
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is his only real disengage/engage tool and it's down for 16-10 seconds depending on rank. Press when it's gone.

playing.title: Look for the level 6 all-in
playing.detail: The Show Stopper slams him down and slows everyone near the landing — use it to drag him off his wave or away from turret range for a clean kill attempt.

playing.title: Play for tempo, not for level 1-5 trades
playing.detail: You're not favored in isolated early trades. Farm safe, force him to spend Fury on the wave, and let Stridebreaker do the talking from level 9-10 onward.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own read of the ability text, not measured data.
